[parcelpoint runtime architecture](<temp>\project\.archi-made-easy\architecture-parcelpoint-20261110-231200\parcelpoint-architecture.html) — open it and use the four guided views (booking path, tracking page, parcel-moved e-mail, shop authentication).

The shape of the system: one Express API owns both the authenticated shop endpoints and the public tracking page, and every asynchronous step hangs off two durable RabbitMQ queues — `shipments.book` into the worker, `parcel.moved` into the notifier. The worker and notifier write/read the same PostgreSQL the API uses, so the database is the real coupling point, and it is single-zone managed with the worker, notifier and broker all at one replica.

Two things that change how you read it:

- It is a runtime/deployment overview, not a file map. The two queues are drawn separately because they have different consumers and opposite failure handling (worker requeues a failed booking; notifier drops a failed e-mail), though both live on the one `rabbitmq` instance from `docker-compose.yml`.
- This directory is not a Git checkout, so there is no commit or origin to pin. File:line evidence is therefore printed as text in the cards instead of clickable, revision-pinned source links. If you point me at the Git working copy (or `git init` + a remote here), I can re-render with hoverable source links.
